evidence_items.locator: Section 4, Othello; Appendix D discussion of Tables 3 and 4
evidence_items.explanation: The synthetic-Othello model passes tests of recognizing equivalent states and distinguishing different states, and maintains nearly error-free legal play under move substitutions. This is stronger counterevidence than a decodable representation, although the same study finds substantial failures in other models and domains.

evidence_items.locator: AI Performance Results; Task-Specific AI Performance

receipt.public_excerpt: world model learning through exploration and experimentation.

evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark reports that Claude 4 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and o3 underperform humans on prediction, planning, and change detection after exploring unfamiliar environments. This supports a practical reliability limitation, but performance also depends on exploration and reasoning, so it does not isolate an inability to induce a world model.

evidence_items.locator: Section 3, model training and chess performance
evidence_items.explanation: Models trained solely to predict chess notation show substantial legal-play competence, alongside board-state probes and interventions. This challenges a simple equation of next-token prediction with having no useful state model, but does not by itself establish the broader reliability required by the contract.

evidence_items.publisher: Yifei Yuan and Anders Søgaard, arXiv

receipt.public_excerpt: predict two or more consecutive moves.

evidence_items.explanation: The study counts illegal generated moves as errors and reports difficulty extending single-move success to consecutive moves. Its simultaneous evidence of learned board representations illustrates why representation recovery alone does not settle reliable functional use.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not establish a common reliability standard connecting successful specialized models to the broader everyday competence discussed in the post.
Failures in the tested systems do not establish that next-token prediction itself is insufficient; success in synthetic Othello does not establish broad everyday reliability.
The evidence does not provide a representative assessment of all relevant capabilities available immediately before the post.
